concept.title: Firefox 154 Gorilla Unleashed - GPU Process Wayland Unblock + Audio/Network Patches Deployed
concept.human_rationale:
[AUDIT VERDICT 2026-08-02 — MOSTLY-TRUE + naming nits] 'media.hardware-video-encoding.failed' is a misnomer — the real dynamic pref is media.hardware-video-decoding.failed (gfxPlatform.cpp:953). kGorillaUploadChunkSize is REAL (lives outside dom/media grep scope).
Today we fixed three critical bottlenecks in the custom Firefox build for the Sony VAIO laptop. First, we discovered the GPU process was being blocked on Wayland, which prevented hardware video decoding from working even though the codec patches were correct. Second, we deployed audio quality patches that lock the sample rate to 48kHz (matching the laptop's Realtek ALC269 hardware) and add a soft limiter to prevent harsh digital clipping. Third, we verified and deployed networking optimizations including a 4MB UDP send buffer, 3-second DNS negative cache, and upload pacing. All 396 patch files were deployed to the Firefox source tree and are ready for rebuild.
PROBLEM: Three interrelated issues prevented the custom Firefox build from achieving its performance targets on the Sony VAIO SVE14A3AJ (Ivy Bridge i7-3632QM, Intel HD 4000, Realtek ALC269, Debian 13 Wayland): (1) GPU process hard-blocked on Wayland via FEATURE_FAILURE_WAYLAND in gfxPlatformGtk.cpp, breaking zero-copy DMABUF frame import and forcing CPU readback copies per frame. (2) Audio patches for 48kHz native rate lock and Fast-Tanh soft limiting existed in the patch folder but were commented out in deploy.sh, so they never reached the source tree. (3) Networking patches for UDP send buffer sizing (4MB), DNS negative TTL reduction (60s->3s), and upload pacing (256KB chunks) needed verification they were actually deployed.
